clauses.reason: The order approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Anti Hog Cholera Serum and Hog Cholera Virus Industry under section 3 of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act: the operative words of the President's order are "do hereby approve said Code of Fair Competition for the Anti-Hog Cholera Serum and Hog Cholera Virus Industry". An approved code had legal effect only through section 3 (under 3(b) its provisions became the standards of fair competition, under 3(c) the district courts could enjoin violations, under 3(f) violations were misdemeanors). Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides: "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". The approval therefore ceased to have operative effect on June 14, 1935. No held record shows this code cancelled or suspended earlier, and June 16, 1935 is not an end because section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936.

inventory_overrides.reason: The machine inventory lists findings 1-5 as five clauses and its item 5 runs on through the whole operative paragraph. Findings 1-4 recite the statutory prerequisites (application, notice, hearings, section 3(a) compliance) and finding 5 recites that the code will tend to effectuate the policy of the Act; none commands anything. The only operative command is the final 'Now, Therefore' paragraph, characters 1717-2031 of the registered text, so the corrected inventory is that one clause.

research_rationale:
EO 6631-A was read in full in the registered APP transcription (common-crawl capture 2025-01-24T06:43:56Z). Identity: the census register row, the WPA 1944 numbered list (1934 Mar 6, p. 570, 'Code of Fair Competition for the Anti-Hog Cholera Serum and Hog Cholera Virus Industry approved') and the APP page record with the same sha256 agree on number, date and subject; the page heading names the order's number, its date matches, and the page record's text_sha256 equals the held file's. The order recites that the Secretary of Agriculture and the Administrator rendered separate reports on the provisions within their respective jurisdictions under Executive Orders 6182, 6207, 6345 and 6551, makes five findings, and then approves the code. The authority it invokes is Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act ('pursuant to the authority vested in me by Title I'), so it is a section 3 code approval and not an instrument issued under the Agricultural Adjustment Act. Under the shared reviewed analysis (SHARED_ANALYSIS.md, ADJUDICATION.json) a code-dependent command that did not end earlier ended on June 14, 1935, when section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 repealed the power to approve or prescribe codes and the provisions enforcing them; Schechter (May 27, 1935) is recorded only as a validity characterization. Original not yet held; the working text is a labeled transcription under the 2026-10-21 owner ruling.
